definitions.gloss: to have no objection; to have no different opinion
definitions.explanation: A formal expression used to indicate agreement or non-opposition to a proposal, decision, or arrangement. Composed of {異存|いぞん} (a differing opinion or objection) + ない (none).

examples.japanese: その{案|あん}に{異存|いぞん}ない。
examples.english: I have no objection to that proposal.

examples.japanese: {皆|みな}さんに{異存|いぞん}がなければ、これで{決定|けってい}します。
examples.english: If no one has any objection, we will finalize it this way.

examples.japanese: {条件|じょうけん}に{異存|いぞん}はございませんが、{契約書|けいやくしょ}の{文言|もんごん}は{再確認|さいかくにん}させてください。
examples.english: I have no objection to the terms, but please let me re-check the wording of the contract.

notes:
A formal, polite way to express agreement. Common in business meetings, contract discussions, and official correspondence.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜に{異存|いぞん}ない: to have no objection to ~
- {異存|いぞん}がなければ: if there is no objection
- {異存|いぞん}はございません: humble form, "I have no objection"
- {異存|いぞん}を{唱|とな}える: to raise an objection (the opposite)

REGISTER:
More formal and written-sounding than {反対|はんたい}しない (don't oppose) or {問題|もんだい}ない (no problem). Often used by superiors or in official settings to signal consent without enthusiasm — a neutral acceptance rather than positive endorsement.
